header.title: Discovering Constant Trig Ratios
header.subtitle: Same angle, same ratio: whatever the size of the triangle

meta.lesson-focus: Investigate nested similar right-angled triangles with a fixed acute angle; measure side ratios systematically and observe that opposite/hypotenuse, adjacent/hypotenuse and opposite/adjacent stay constant for that angle; connect to the unit-hypotenuse triangle.
meta.ac9-descriptor-text: recognise the constancy of the sine, cosine and tangent ratios for a given angle in right-angled triangles using properties of similarity
meta.sa-conceptual-understanding: Trigonometric ratios are an application of the property of similarity for right-angled triangles

html.section0_intro: Last lesson you named the sides of a right-angled triangle, and earlier you met enlargement. Three quick questions to warm those ideas up.
html.section_warmup:
A real situation that is secretly today's mathematics.

A shed company sells three sizes of garden shed: small, medium and large. Every shed has the same roof pitch (the angle the roof makes with the horizontal), but bigger sheds have longer roofs.

The rafter timber costs $12.50 per metre. The estimator never measures a rafter. She measures the rise of the roof and doubles it. Small shed: rise 1 m, rafter 2 m. Medium: rise 1.5 m, rafter 3 m. Large: rise 2 m, rafter 4 m.

Why does one shortcut work for every size of shed?

For the roof angle θ, the rise is the opposite side and the rafter is the hypotenuse. On every shed, rise ÷ rafter = 0.5. Today you discover why: when the angle stays the same, the ratio of two sides stays the same, however big the triangle is.
html.vocab_cards:
Similar triangles
Tap to flip
Triangles with the same angles. One is an enlargement of the other, so every side is multiplied by the same scale factor.
A 3-4-5 and a 6-8-10 triangle are similar.
Nested triangles
Tap to flip
Similar triangles drawn inside one another, sharing one angle and lined up along the same two lines.
Like a set of stacking triangles.
Corresponding sides
Tap to flip
Sides that are in the same position in two similar triangles, e.g. the two hypotenuses.
Both are opposite the same angle.
Side ratio
Tap to flip
One side length divided by another side of the same triangle.
opposite ÷ hypotenuse = 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6
Unit-hypotenuse triangle
Tap to flip
The similar triangle whose hypotenuse is exactly 1 unit long. Its other two sides equal the ratios.
A 3-4-5 triangle shrinks to 0.6, 0.8, 1.
html.section3_heading: Enlarge it: what changes, what stays the same?
html.section3_desc: A right-angled triangle is enlarged by scale factor 3. The angle θ is kept the same. Drag each card into Changes or Stays the same.
html.sort_activity:
Triangle ABC is enlarged by scale factor 3 (θ stays at A)
Length of the hypotenuse Size of the angle θ Length of the opposite side opposite ÷ hypotenuse The perimeter The right angle adjacent ÷ hypotenuse The area opposite ÷ adjacent

Changes

Stays the same

💡 Every length is multiplied by 3, so 3 cm becomes 9 cm and 5 cm becomes 15 cm. But 9 ÷ 15 = 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6: the scale factor appears on the top and the bottom, so it cancels. Angles and side ratios never change under enlargement.
html.section4_heading: Match the triangles with the same angle θ
html.worked_example:
Three right-angled triangles are nested inside each other on a grid. They all share the angle θ at A. Do their side ratios depend on the size of the triangle?

1
Measure the sides systematically
For θ at A, the vertical side is opposite, the side along the x-axis is adjacent, and the sloping side is the hypotenuse. Count the grid squares for opposite and adjacent; Pythagoras gives the hypotenuse.
Triangleoppositeadjacenthypotenuse
ABC345
ADE6810
AFG91215
2
Calculate the three ratios for each triangle
Divide within each triangle, always in the same order.
Triangleoppositehypotenuseadjacenthypotenuseoppositeadjacent
ABC35 = 0.645 = 0.834 = 0.75
ADE610 = 0.6810 = 0.868 = 0.75
AFG915 = 0.61215 = 0.8912 = 0.75
3
Explain the pattern and shrink to hypotenuse 1
The triangles are similar: ADE is ABC enlarged by 2, AFG by 3. Each ratio is (k × side) ÷ (k × side), so the scale factor k cancels. The ratios belong to the angle, not to the triangle. Shrink ABC by scale factor 15 and its hypotenuse is 1 unit: the opposite side is then 0.6 and the adjacent side is 0.8, exactly the two ratios.
Unit-hypotenuse triangle for this θ:   opposite = 0.6, adjacent = 0.8, hypotenuse = 1
html.section6_heading: We do: two nested triangles, one angle
html.we_do_intro: Triangles ABC and ADE share the angle θ at A. Work through each prompt with a partner, then we check as a class. Fractions or exact decimals are both fine.
html.strategy_section:
★Explore: fix the angle, change the size

Drag the size slider and watch the three ratios. Then drag the angle slider. Which slider changes the ratios? The dashed triangle is the unit-hypotenuse triangle for the same angle.

opposite3.01
adjacent3.99
hypotenuse5.00
opposite ÷ hypotenuse0.602
adjacent ÷ hypotenuse0.799
opposite ÷ adjacent0.754

🎯 Challenge

Use the angle slider to make opposite ÷ hypotenuse = 0.5. Then change the size: does the ratio move?

💡 What to notice: the size slider changes every length but none of the ratios. Only the angle changes the ratios. Set the hypotenuse to 1 and the opposite and adjacent sides read off the ratios directly.

★Hinge check 🎯 Pick one

Triangle Q is triangle P enlarged by scale factor 3. Both have the same angle θ at A. Which statement is true?

P
Q
Not quite. Both the opposite side and the hypotenuse were multiplied by 3. 9 ÷ 15 = 0.6 and 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6: the 3s cancel, so the ratio does not change.
Correct. 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6 and 9 ÷ 15 = 0.6. Enlarging multiplies the top and the bottom of the ratio by the same scale factor, so the ratio stays the same for that angle.
That's thinking additively. The sides grew by multiplying, not adding. Work out 9 ÷ 15 and compare it with 3 ÷ 5.
Enlargement never changes angles. Similar triangles have exactly the same angles; only the lengths change. That is why their side ratios match.

retrieval.q: In triangle ABC the right angle is at C and θ is at A. Which side is opposite θ? Type the two letters in alphabetical order.
retrieval.hint: The opposite side does not touch A at all.

fb.AB: AB is across from the right angle, so it is the hypotenuse.

retrieval.q: A triangle with sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm is enlarged by scale factor 4. How long is the longest side of the image, in cm?
retrieval.hint: Enlargement multiplies every length by the scale factor: 5 × 4.

fb.9: You added 4. Enlargement multiplies every side by the scale factor.

retrieval.q: Write 915 as a decimal.
retrieval.hint: Simplify first: 9 ÷ 3 = 3 and 15 ÷ 3 = 5, so it is 3 ÷ 5.

In the small triangle ABC, what is oppositehypotenuse? Type a fraction (e.g. 5/13) or an exact decimal.
weDo.hint: Opposite θ is BC = 5; the hypotenuse is AC = 13.

fb.5/12: That is opposite ÷ adjacent. This one divides by the hypotenuse.

weDo.q: In the large triangle ADE, what is oppositehypotenuse? Compare it with your first answer. Type a fraction (e.g. 5/13) or an exact decimal.
weDo.hint: Opposite θ is DE = 10; the hypotenuse is AE = 26. Simplify 10/26.

weDo.q: A third triangle with the same angle θ has hypotenuse 39 cm. Use the ratio to find its opposite side, in cm.
weDo.hint: opposite ÷ hypotenuse = 5/13 for this angle, so opposite = 5/13 × 39.

fb.36: 36 is the adjacent side (12/13 × 39). Use opposite ÷ hypotenuse = 5/13.

checkpoint.q: For θ at A, what is oppositehypotenuse? Type a fraction (e.g. 5/13) or an exact decimal.
checkpoint.hint: Opposite θ is BC; the hypotenuse is AB.

fb.0.75: 6 ÷ 8 is opposite ÷ adjacent. Divide the opposite side by the hypotenuse, AB.
fb.0.8: 8 ÷ 10 is adjacent ÷ hypotenuse. Use the side opposite θ.

checkpoint.q: Another right-angled triangle has the same angle θ and a hypotenuse of 25 cm. How long is its opposite side, in cm?
checkpoint.hint: The ratio opposite ÷ hypotenuse is still 0.6, so opposite = 0.6 × 25.

fb.21: You added 15 to 6, like the hypotenuse grew by 15. Enlargement multiplies: use the ratio 0.6 × 25.

practice1.q: For θ at A, what is oppositehypotenuse? Type a fraction (e.g. 5/13) or an exact decimal.
practice1.hint: Opposite θ is BC = 3; the hypotenuse is AC = 5.

fb.0.75: 3 ÷ 4 is opposite ÷ adjacent. Divide by the hypotenuse.

practice1.q: For θ at A, what is adjacenthypotenuse? Type a fraction (e.g. 5/13) or an exact decimal.
practice1.hint: Adjacent to θ is AB = 4; the hypotenuse is AC = 5.

fb.0.6: 3 ÷ 5 uses the opposite side. Adjacent is the side touching θ that isn't the hypotenuse.

practice1.q: For θ at A, what is oppositeadjacent? Type a fraction (e.g. 5/13) or an exact decimal.
practice1.hint: Opposite is BC = 3; adjacent is AB = 4.

practice1.q: For θ at R, what is oppositehypotenuse? Type a fraction (e.g. 5/13) or an exact decimal.
practice1.hint: θ is at R. The side that does not touch R is PQ = 5; the hypotenuse is PR = 13.

fb.12/13: 12 ÷ 13 uses QR, which touches θ: that's adjacent ÷ hypotenuse.

practice1.q: For θ at R, what is oppositeadjacent? Type a fraction (e.g. 5/13) or an exact decimal.
practice1.hint: Opposite is PQ = 5; adjacent is QR = 12.

practice1.q: For θ at F, what is adjacenthypotenuse? Type a fraction (e.g. 5/13) or an exact decimal.
practice1.hint: θ is at F. EF touches F and the right angle, so EF = 15 is adjacent. The hypotenuse is DF = 17.

fb.8/17: DE does not touch F, so it is the opposite side. Use the adjacent side EF.

practice1.q: For θ at L, what is oppositehypotenuse? Compare it with your answer to P1. Type a fraction (e.g. 5/13) or an exact decimal.
practice1.hint: Opposite θ is JK = 6; the hypotenuse is JL = 10.

fb.0.8: 8 ÷ 10 is adjacent ÷ hypotenuse. Use JK, the side that does not touch L.

practice1.q: This triangle has the same angle θ as triangle ABC in P1, so oppositehypotenuse = 0.6. How long is BC, in cm?

fb.33.3: You divided 20 by 0.6. The opposite side is shorter than the hypotenuse: multiply.

practice1.q: For this angle θ, adjacenthypotenuse = 0.8. How long is AB, in cm?
For this angle θ, oppositeadjacent = 0.75. How long is BC, in cm?

fb.26.7: You divided by 0.75. Opposite = 0.75 × adjacent, so multiply.

practice2.q: For θ at X, what is oppositehypotenuse? Type a fraction (e.g. 5/13) or an exact decimal.
practice2.hint: θ is at X. YZ = 24 does not touch X, so it is opposite; XZ = 25 is the hypotenuse.

fb.7/25: XY touches X, so it is adjacent. The opposite side is YZ.

practice2.q: Now use the other acute angle α at Z. What is opposite ÷ adjacent for α? Type a fraction (e.g. 5/13) or an exact decimal.
practice2.hint: From Z, the side that does not touch Z is XY = 7 (opposite). YZ = 24 touches Z and the right angle (adjacent).

fb.24/7: That is opposite ÷ adjacent for the angle at X. From Z, opposite and adjacent swap.

practice2.q: A right-angled triangle has opposite 9 cm, adjacent 12 cm and hypotenuse 15 cm. In the unit-hypotenuse triangle with the same angle θ, how long is the adjacent side?
practice2.hint: Divide by 15 so the hypotenuse becomes 1: adjacent = 12 ÷ 15.

practice2.q: A straight line starts at the origin O and passes through (4, 3). Dropping a vertical from any point on the line to the x-axis makes a right-angled triangle with the same angle θ at O. The point (20, y) is on the line. Find y.
practice2.hint: opposite ÷ adjacent = 3 ÷ 4 = 0.75 for every point on the line, so y = 0.75 × 20.

fb.19: You added 16 to 3, matching x going from 4 to 20. Points on the line scale by multiplying: 20 is 5 × 4.

fb.9.6: You divided by 0.5. The rise is shorter than the rafter: multiply by 0.5.

practice3.q: A shed with the same pitch (rise ÷ rafter = 0.5) has a rise of 1.5 m. Its roof needs 8 rafters, and rafter timber costs $12.50 per metre. What is the total cost of the rafters, in dollars?
practice3.hint: rafter = 1.5 ÷ 0.5 = 3 m. Total timber = 8 × 3 = 24 m. Cost = 24 × 12.50.

fb.150: A rafter is 1.5 ÷ 0.5 = 3 m, not 1.5 m. Find the rafter length first.

practice3.q: A building code says a wheelchair ramp must have rise ÷ run (opposite ÷ adjacent) of 1/14. A ramp must rise 0.35 m. How long is its horizontal run, in metres?

fb.0.025: You divided 0.35 by 14. The run is much longer than the rise: multiply by 14.

practice3.q: At 4 pm a student 1.6 m tall casts a 2 m shadow. At the same moment a tree casts a 15 m shadow. The sun makes the same angle with the ground for both. How tall is the tree, in metres?
practice3.hint: height ÷ shadow = 1.6 ÷ 2 = 0.8 for both, so tree = 0.8 × 15.

fb.14.6: You added 13 to 1.6, matching the shadow growing by 13 m. Same angle means same ratio: multiply.

exitProbs.q: For θ at G, what is oppositehypotenuse? Type a fraction (e.g. 5/13) or an exact decimal.
exitProbs.hint: Opposite θ is HK = 12; the hypotenuse is GK = 20.

fb.0.75: 12 ÷ 16 is opposite ÷ adjacent. Divide by the hypotenuse GK.

exitProbs.q: A different right-angled triangle has the same angle θ and a hypotenuse of 35 cm. How long is its opposite side, in cm?
exitProbs.hint: opposite ÷ hypotenuse = 0.6 for this angle, so opposite = 0.6 × 35.

exitProbs.q: Explain why opposite ÷ hypotenuse is the same for every right-angled triangle with the same angle θ, no matter how big the triangle is.
exitProbs.hint: Think about what enlargement does to both sides, and what happens to the scale factor when you divide.
